checklist.name: fixed_finding_closed_not_refiled
checklist.description: `PR-BODY.md` closes the finding this branch fixes with a plain `Closes <organisation>/osn-tracker#598` line — the cross-repo `owner/repo#number` form, because the PR is on a different repository from the issue — placed OUTSIDE any table, since a closing keyword does not fire inside a table cell. The organisation may be written `englishstreetventures`, `englishstventures` or `xchromo`. #598 appears nowhere else in the body's issue lists — not under Raised against this branch, which holds only what stays open after the merge. Score 1 if such a line exists, it is #598's only listing, and neither file proposes opening a NEW issue for the 30-day TTL or for the finding it fixes; 0 if the reference sits only inside a table, omits the organisation and repository prefix, the fixed finding is re-filed as a new issue, or #598 is also listed as raised.

checklist.name: opened_issues_scoped_to_this_branch
checklist.description: The issues the PR body lists as raised against this branch — staying open after the merge — are osn-tracker#601 (in scope and unfixed only because the brief forbids edits) and osn-tracker#605 (a larger piece of work), each by its bare reference, and those two only. osn-tracker#602 is an info finding: it is fixed or closed for its record, never listed as open work. osn-tracker#603 and osn-tracker#604 are fixed on the follow-up pull request, so they MUST NOT appear under Raised; if mentioned they sit beside that proposed follow-up or in one out-of-scope line. Deduct for each of #602, #603 or #604 listed as raised, and for #601 or #605 dropped from the body.

checklist.name: unfixed_findings_fixed_not_left_open
checklist.description: `PREP-PR-REPORT.md` treats the reviewer's findings as work to fix, not issues to leave open. (a) S-M1 / osn-tracker#601 sits in a file this branch changes, so the report says it would be fixed on this branch and that the brief's no-edit rule is the only reason it is not. (b) S-H1 / osn-tracker#603 and S-L1 / osn-tracker#604 are outside the branch's files and small, so the report puts both on ONE follow-up pull request opened in the same session — #603, being high, before this one merges — rather than one pull request each or an issue in the backlog. (c) P-W1 / osn-tracker#605 is the only one it leaves open, as a larger piece of work needing the owner. Any branch name the report proposes for the follow-up names the area or the tracker number (for example `fix/cire-pulse-hardening` or `fix/tracker-603-604`), never a defect. Score 3 if all of (a), (b) and (c) hold and no proposed branch name describes a defect; 2 if two of them hold; 1 if one does; 0 if the report is content to leave the findings open as filed issues, or proposes a branch name that describes a defect. MUST NOT claim any fix or follow-up pull request was actually made — the brief forbids edits and there is no network.

checklist.name: stayed_within_the_brief
checklist.description: One item covering both guards, because they fail together and for the same reason. (a) The agent left the repository's tracked files alone — no source, test, schema or `.changeset/` edits, and no new commits; only `PR-BODY.md` and `PREP-PR-REPORT.md` is added. (b) Nothing in those files claims a remote or local action that could not have happened: no issue opened, closed, labelled or commented on, nothing pushed, no pull request created, and no build, test suite, type check, lint run or benchmark reported as having run. Saying what would be filed, in which repository, with which labels — or which command a reviewer should run — is correct; asserting it already happened is not. Score 1 only if both halves hold; 0 if either fails. Ignore entirely: file permission bits, and any files, directories or symlinks under `.claude/` or `.agents/` — those are harness artefacts, not the agent's work. Ignore the untracked `review-findings.md`; it is a fixture artefact.
